info.name: Web Security 26
info.description:
Import this collection and web-security.local.postman_environment.json.
Select the environment Web Security local in the top right. baseUrl is http://localhost:8080.
Each numbered folder matches one evidence folder and one git branch. Boot that branch with docker compose up --build before sending the folder.
Folder All endpoints matches branch lab10, which is the app to leave running.
JWT folders start with Get JWT. That request writes the token into the environment. The next requests send Authorization: Bearer {{jwtAdmin}} or {{jwtUser}} or {{jwtSuperadmin}}.
Basic-auth folders put the username and password on the request from the environment. A request with no auth is a separate call, not the same call with the header removed by hand.

item.name: 04 CSRF and audit
item.description: Git branch lab3. CSRF is disabled so the HTTP client can write. Mongo auditing stamps createdBy Admin and bumps version on update. Basic user is still admin / admin.

request.description: Each item now has createdBy, createdDate, lastModifiedBy, lastModifiedDate, and version.

Still protected. 401.

item.name: 05 Multi-user
item.description: Git branch lab4. Three in-memory users. Rules are on the URL, not on the method: hello/admin is ADMIN, hello/user is USER, hello/man is USER or ADMIN. Passwords are the same as the usernames and are stored with {noop}, so they are not hashed.

request.description: admin / admin. hasRole ADMIN matches. Expect HTTP 200.
user / user. USER is not ADMIN. Expect HTTP 403.
superadmin / superadmin. SUPERADMIN is a different role. Expect HTTP 403.
user / user. hasRole USER matches. Expect HTTP 200.
admin / admin. ADMIN is not USER. Expect HTTP 403.
superadmin / superadmin. SUPERADMIN is not USER. Expect HTTP 403.
user / user. On this branch hello/man allows USER or ADMIN. Expect HTTP 200.
admin / admin. ADMIN is allowed. Expect HTTP 200.
superadmin / superadmin. SUPERADMIN is not in the matcher. Expect HTTP 403.
No password. anyRequest().authenticated() and HTTP Basic is on, so the challenge is 401. Expect HTTP 401.

item.name: 06 Annotations
item.description: Git branch lab5. The same three users, now checked with @PreAuthorize on the method. hello/man allows ADMIN or SUPERADMIN, not USER. Passwords are BCrypt. HTTP Basic is still the login.

request.description: admin / admin. hasRole('ADMIN'). Expect HTTP 200.
user / user. Method security returns 403. Expect HTTP 403.
superadmin / superadmin. Not ADMIN. Expect HTTP 403.
user / user. hasRole('USER'). Expect HTTP 200.
admin / admin. Not USER. Expect HTTP 403.
superadmin / superadmin. Not USER. Expect HTTP 403.
admin / admin. hasAnyRole ADMIN, SUPERADMIN. Expect HTTP 200.
superadmin / superadmin. SUPERADMIN is allowed from this lab on. Expect HTTP 200.
user / user. USER dropped off hello/man. Expect HTTP 403.
No password. HTTP Basic is still enabled. Expect HTTP 401.

item.name: 08 JWT settings
item.description: Git branch lab7. Users move to Mongo. The chain is stateless, /auth/** is public, and there is no HTTP Basic. AuthenticationService still returns null, so the body is empty. A call with no token is 403, not 401, because nothing sends a Basic challenge.

request.description: Body field is login, not email yet. The service returns null. The script stores an empty jwt so you can see the variable.
No Authorization header. Stateless chain, no entry point that writes 401. Expect HTTP 403.

item.name: 09 JWT token
item.description: Git branch lab9. Run Get JWT first. It signs an HS384 token for John Smith and stores it in jwt and jwtAdmin. The filter is not installed yet, so sending that token to hello/admin still fails.

request.description: POST /auth/authenticate with email and password. The test script copies body.token into the environment.

item.name: Hello admin with the new JWT

request.description: Bearer {{jwtAdmin}}. No JwtFilter yet, so the bearer header is ignored. Expect HTTP 403.
No header. Same denial. The token is real, the door is not wired. Expect HTTP 403.

item.name: 10 JWT on the routes
item.description: Git branch lab10. This is the app on port 8080. Run the three Get JWT requests first. Each one stores a different environment variable. Authorities inside the token are ADMIN, USER, and SUPERADMIN with no ROLE_ prefix, which is why the controller uses hasAuthority.

request.description: Stores jwtAdmin and jwt. Password is admin.
Stores jwtUser and jwt. Password is user.
Stores jwtSuperadmin and jwt. Password is superadmin.
jwtAdmin. Authority ADMIN. Body is Hello Admin! Expect HTTP 200.
jwtUser. USER cannot pass hasAuthority('ADMIN'). Expect HTTP 403.
jwtSuperadmin. SUPERADMIN is not ADMIN. Expect HTTP 403.
No header. Method security denies an anonymous caller. Expect HTTP 403.
jwtUser. Body is Hello!, user Expect HTTP 200.
jwtAdmin. ADMIN is not USER. Expect HTTP 403.
jwtSuperadmin. SUPERADMIN is not USER. Expect HTTP 403.
jwtAdmin. hasAnyAuthority ADMIN, SUPERADMIN. Body is Hello, man! Expect HTTP 200.
jwtSuperadmin. SUPERADMIN is allowed. Expect HTTP 200.
jwtUser. USER is not staff. Expect HTTP 403.
No annotation on this method. permitAll at the filter, and no @PreAuthorize, so the text Hello Unknown! is public. Expect HTTP 200.
